tagline.text: A southern Cebu town linking the Casay beach park and the vegetable fields of the Mantalongon highlands

location.label: Location
location.text: Southeastern coast of Cebu Island, a municipality about 84 km south of Cebu City

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱600~2,500 (per person, based on a day trip from Cebu City including transport, fees and meals)

children.text: Dalaguete is a town running from the southeastern coast of Cebu up to the Mantalongon highlands, with a white-sand beach park, a cool mountain village known as the "Little Baguio of Cebu," and the starting point for the Osmeña Peak trek. You can taste both sea and mountains in one day.

Dalaguete is a coastal municipality about 84 km south of Cebu City. The 2024 census counted about 76,000 residents in 33 barangays over roughly 155 square kilometers. The name is said to come from the dalakit tree (Ficus benjamina) that stood here; even before the Spanish arrived, people gathered under it to socialize and trade, and after the Spanish built a church on the spot, the town grew. The church of St. William of Aquitaine was founded in 1711. Geographically it borders Argao to the north, Badian and Alegria to the west and Alcoy to the south, with the Cebu Strait to the east. This position makes it a convenient stop on a trip across southern Cebu and also a starting point for mountain roads over to the west coast (Moalboal and Kawasan).

What Dalaguete offers travelers is that coast and mountains lie within one municipality. On the coast is the Dalaguete Beach Park (Casay Beach) run by the local government, and inland stretch the Mantalongon highlands. Thanks to its cool climate, Mantalongon is called the "Little Baguio of Cebu" and the "Summer Capital of Cebu," and Dalaguete is called the "Vegetable Basket of Cebu" for its lively vegetable farming. The highland vegetables sold in the market and the cool mist define the impression of this town.

For trekkers, it is best known as the starting point for Osmeña Peak. This peak, introduced as the highest in Cebu at 1,013 m above sea level, is climbed from the Mantalongon area, and from the top you see ridges of limestone peaks and, across the sea, Negros Island (some sources place the peak on the Badian border, so check on a map app). This guide covers the coastal park, Mantalongon and the Osmeña Peak entrance as one town.

It is closer to a full day of nature travel than city sightseeing. Leave Cebu City early in the morning to see Mantalongon and Osmeña Peak, then come down to the coast in the afternoon and rest at Casay Beach for a full day. However, the motorcycle-taxi transfers between the two points take a long time and the views change greatly with weather and fog, so keep the schedule loose. If you camp on the mountain, the ground is loose enough that you must tie the tent to a large rock with rope, and thick fog sets in by evening, so bring warm clothing. Use a campsite a few meters below the summit rather than right on top; the campsite caretaker collects the trash.

This cool mountain village, called the "Little Baguio of Cebu," has vegetable fields and misty ridges. You can buy vegetables and fruit at the market, and it is a good place to eat breakfast or shop before heading to Osmeña Peak.
This is a white-sand beach run by the local government in Barangay Casay. It is about
1.5 km
off the national road; per 2018 and 2020 guides, admission was about

and has no overnight accommodation. Check current fees locally.
Founded in 1711, this parish church is the symbol of the town center. It is nice for a light look at the old stone structure and for connecting the market and restaurants around the plaza.
True to a vegetable-growing area, the market is rich in highland vegetables and fruit. Buying light food and eating it at the beach or a viewpoint is a popular way among local travelers.
A traverse from Osmeña Peak to Kawasan Falls in Badian is known. The descent takes about 4–6 hours, so plan it with a guide.
The town festival honoring the patron saint San Guillermo is held on
around February 9–10

. The highlight is the street-dance competition called the "Utanon Festival." The saint's feast day is February 10, but in some years (e.g. 2016) it was held a day earlier, so dates may change from year to year.
Casay Beach faces east, so the sunrise view is good. At Osmeña Peak some trekkers also look for sunrise and sunset, but on thick-fog days the view is blocked, so check the weather forecast.

items.title: Day route
items.subtitle: From mountain to sea in one day

children.text: Take a bus bound for Dalaguete from the Cebu South Bus Terminal in Cebu City.
At the Dalaguete junction, take a motorcycle taxi up to Mantalongon.
Register at the Mantalongon Barangay Hall, then go to the Osmeña Peak entrance.
Enjoy the ridge, the limestone peaks and the sea view near the top.
Have lunch at the Mantalongon market and come down to the coast.
Rest and take photos at Casay Beach Park.
Catch a bus back to Cebu City.
Check the last bus and motorcycle-taxi times in advance, and shorten the summit plans if fog or rain is heavy.
Register in Mantalongon and climb Osmeña Peak.
Camp at the site below the summit, preparing for fog and cold.
After sunrise, start the traverse down toward Kawasan Falls.
Arrive at Kawasan Falls, rest and check transport for the return.
Camping and the traverse need gear and a guide, so get local advice and check the weather.
Direct flights run daily from Manila's Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB) and take about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Check airlines and schedules when booking.
From the airport to the Cebu South Bus Terminal in Cebu City takes about
30 minutes to 1 hour
by taxi or Grab.
At the Cebu South Bus Terminal, take a bus bound for Oslob, Santander, Alcoy or Bato and get off in the Dalaguete direction. It takes about
2–3 hours
, and the fare is reported at about
It is usual to get off at the junction for Casay Beach and then take a tricycle or motorcycle taxi about
1.5 km
(ordinary vs. aircon; 2026 guide sites).
For Mantalongon, one way is to get off the bus at the Dalaguete junction and ride up by motorcycle taxi, or to take a minibus from the gas station near Carbon Market to the Mantalongon market.
Fares and routes may change, so check at the terminal.
From the Mantalongon market to the peak entrance, you ride up the rough road by motorcycle or walk for about
1–2 hours
. From the entrance to the summit it is about
30 minutes
on foot.
There is a place along the way to get water, but it may dry up in the dry season, so bring plenty.
By car or taxi it is about
84 km
from Cebu City. The section to the Osmeña Peak entrance has unpaved stretches that may be hard for an ordinary car.

Dalaguete has the tropical climate of southern Cebu, and Mantalongon is cooler than the lowlands thanks to its altitude. Trekking is better in the dry season, and in the rain the paths are slippery and dangerous.
The beach park is quiet on weekdays and crowded on weekends and holidays. To see sunrise or sunset at the peak you must go up early, and bring a jacket for evening fog and cold.

The beach park of Dalaguete has no accommodation; there are small guesthouses, homestays and resorts in town, in Mantalongon and along the nearby coast. Many people who want sunrise at Osmeña Peak stay overnight in Mantalongon or nearby and climb before dawn. Lodging names and rates change by season, so check booking sites and reviews.

Food centers on Cebuano dishes and fresh vegetables at the market and restaurants. At Casay Beach you can bring a packed meal or buy from shops in the park. On the mountain it is better to prepare lunch separately or buy it at the Mantalongon market beforehand.
When getting off the bus, tell the conductor in advance that you will get off at the Dalaguete junction (or the Casay entrance).
Osmeña Peak is busiest around sunrise and sunset, so aim for a weekday daytime or early morning.
Mantalongon is cool and foggy, so bring a thin jacket and a raincoat.
The trekking path has slippery stretches, so wear shoes with good grip.
The beach park gets crowded on weekends, so go on a weekday and take your trash with you.
Carry water in large bottles and refill at the first water source.
Do the Kawasan traverse with a guide and check the last bus time home.
Prepare insect repellent, a hat and sun protection.

On the trail there are stretches with no water for hours after the water source, so fill large empty bottles before leaving. The last bus home from the Kawasan side is reported to leave around 8 p.m., so time your descent accordingly.
The mountain paths are very slippery in rain and fog, and the road is rough. On bad-weather days, give up the summit plan.
The summit and campsite turn sharply cold at night and fog is thick, so thermal gear is needed.
You may meet snakes and dogs on the trail, so be careful.
Ask motorcycle taxis for a helmet, and avoid reckless speed on rough roads.
Entrance fees and bus fares come from older sources and may have changed, so check locally.

, a trekking spot at 1,013 m, connects from Mantalongon.

in Badian to the west is the destination of the traverse from Osmeña Peak.
Moalboal
on the west coast is famous for diving and sardine shoals and pairs well with Dalaguete in a southern trip.
Oslob
to the south is known for whale shark tours.
